claim: after his death Clive Paton took material to Martinborough
because: Clive Paton bought young Abel-clone vines (about 3,000 cuttings) from Malcolm Abel in 1980 while Abel was alive, and planted them at Ata Rangi. He worked the 1981 vintage with Abel, who died suddenly in 1981. The explanation reverses that order.
fix: in 1980, shortly before Abel's sudden death in 1981, Clive Paton bought vines from him and planted them in Martinborough
